recognize_zh: 一群大型細胞成簇排列，核圓偏位於細胞一端，胞質豐富淡藍呈泡沫狀，並可見與核分開的淡染區（遠離核的 hof），外觀像大型漿細胞但核染色質較細緻，這就是骨髓中的造骨細胞（osteoblast）。
features: Cohesive cluster of large cells, larger than plasma cells
Round to oval eccentric nuclei with fine to moderately condensed chromatin and small nucleoli
Abundant pale to medium blue, slightly foamy cytoplasm with ill-defined borders
Pale perinuclear clearing (Golgi zone) located away from the nucleus
Background of normal hematopoietic cells, including a neutrophil, lymphocytes, and platelets
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows a cohesive cluster of large cells with round eccentric nuclei, fine chromatin, small nucleoli, and abundant pale blue foamy cytoplasm with a pale clear zone separated from the nucleus. The cells are larger than plasma cells and lack the clock-face chromatin of plasma cells. Background hematopoietic elements are unremarkable. Findings are consistent with osteoblasts, a normal marrow constituent more frequently seen in aspirates from children or areas of active bone remodeling.

ddx.vs: Plasma cells are smaller with clock-face chromatin and a perinuclear hof immediately adjacent to the nucleus, whereas the osteoblast Golgi zone lies away from the nucleus.
Carcinoma clusters show nuclear pleomorphism, prominent nucleoli, and molding, and are cytokeratin positive, unlike the bland uniform osteoblasts.
Osteoclasts are multinucleated giant cells with many separate nuclei, whereas each osteoblast has a single nucleus.
Mast cells contain dense purple metachromatic granules obscuring the nucleus.
